children: The payments major offloaded a 4.31 per cent holding through 13 block transactions on the BSE, with domestic and foreign institutional investors picking up the shares, according to media reports
Mastercard has exited fintech company Pine Labs after selling its entire 4.31 per cent stake for Rs 933.57 crore through a series of block deals on the BSE, according to media reports.

Mastercard Asia/Pacific Pte Ltd, an affiliate of the US-based payments major, sold 4,97,24,182 shares of Noida-based Pine Labs in 13 separate transactions at an average price of Rs 187.75 per share, as per media reports.
A group of mutual funds managed by Kotak Mahindra, Edelweiss and Franklin Templeton, along with ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company, acquired an equivalent number of shares at the same price.

The buyers also included several foreign institutional investors, including Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Citigroup Global Markets Singapore, BNP Paribas Arbitrage, Ghisallo Capital Management, Rams Equities Portfolio Fund, Societe Generale, Susquehanna International Group and NRSGVCC.

The Mastercard stake sale comes amid a series of secondary transactions involving Pine Labs investors this year. In June, financial services firm Actis sold a little over 2 per cent stake in the fintech company for Rs 371 crore.
Earlier in the same month, Actis Pine Labs Investment Holdings had sold nearly 1 per cent of its holding for Rs 152 crore. Actis is part of global growth investor General Atlantic.
